as_told.title: Schoch and Hancock: the Sphinx as an homage to Leo

plain: The Great Sphinx at Giza looked straight at the constellation Leo at sunrise on the spring equinox about 12,500 years ago, not 4,500, which would make the monument far older than usually thought. The writer Graham Hancock tells Michels this himself, crediting the writer Robert Bauval and tying it to the three stars of Orion's belt lining up due south at the same moment, and the researcher Randall Carlson repeats it as dating work by Bauval and Hancock. Michels himself credits Hancock and the geologist Robert Schoch instead, and puts it as the Sphinx being carved as a lion in honour of the age of Leo, an age set by the slow wobble of Earth's axis.
